entries.ex: Air *pollution* in large cities is linked to asthma and heart disease.
entries.exAr: يرتبط *تلوث* الهواء في المدن الكبرى بالربو وأمراض القلب.

entries.ex: Factories must cut their carbon *emissions* by 40% within ten years.
entries.exAr: يجب على المصانع خفض *انبعاثاتها* الكربونية بنسبة ٤٠٪ خلال عشر سنوات.

entries.ex: Methane is a powerful *greenhouse gas* produced partly by livestock farming.
entries.exAr: الميثان *غاز دفيئة* قوي ينتج جزئيًا عن تربية المواشي.

entries.ex: Scientists agree that *global warming* is largely caused by human activity.
entries.exAr: يتفق العلماء على أن *الاحترار العالمي* ناجم إلى حد كبير عن النشاط البشري.

entries.ex: Farmers are already feeling the effects of *climate change* through shorter rainy seasons.
entries.exAr: يشعر المزارعون بالفعل بآثار *تغير المناخ* من خلال قِصَر مواسم الأمطار.

entries.ex: *Deforestation* in the Amazon destroys the habitats of countless species.
entries.exAr: تدمر *إزالة الغابات* في منطقة الأمازون موائل أنواع لا تحصى من الكائنات.

entries.ex: Removing a single predator can upset the balance of an entire *ecosystem*.
entries.exAr: قد يؤدي القضاء على مفترس واحد إلى اختلال توازن *نظام بيئي* بأكمله.

entries.ex: Wildlife *conservation* projects have helped tiger numbers to grow again.
entries.exAr: ساعدت مشروعات *الحفاظ* على الحياة البرية على عودة أعداد النمور إلى الازدياد.

entries.ex: Solar and wind power offer a more *sustainable* source of energy than coal.
entries.exAr: توفر الطاقة الشمسية وطاقة الرياح مصدرًا *أكثر استدامة* للطاقة من الفحم.

entries.ex: Most households in the city now *recycle* their glass, paper and plastic.
entries.exAr: تقوم معظم الأسر في المدينة الآن *بإعادة تدوير* الزجاج والورق والبلاستيك.

entries.ex: Restaurants throw away tonnes of food *waste* every week.
entries.exAr: تتخلص المطاعم من أطنان من *مخلفات* الطعام كل أسبوع.

entries.ex: Plastic bags can stay in a *landfill* for hundreds of years without breaking down.
entries.exAr: يمكن أن تبقى الأكياس البلاستيكية في *مكب النفايات* مئات السنين دون أن تتحلل.

entries.ex: Chemicals from the factory *contaminated* the river that supplies the town's water.
entries.exAr: *لوّثت* المواد الكيميائية الصادرة عن المصنع النهر الذي يزود البلدة بالمياه.

entries.ex: A long *drought* has caused crop failures across the region.
entries.exAr: تسبب *جفاف* طويل في تلف المحاصيل في أرجاء المنطقة.

entries.ex: Heavy rain caused a *flood* that forced thousands of families to leave their homes.
entries.exAr: تسببت الأمطار الغزيرة في *فيضان* أجبر آلاف الأسر على مغادرة منازلها.

entries.ex: Taking the train instead of short flights can greatly reduce your *carbon footprint*.
entries.exAr: يمكن أن يقلل ركوب القطار بدلًا من الرحلات الجوية القصيرة *بصمتك الكربونية* كثيرًا.

entries.ex: *Environmentalists* have campaigned for years to protect the coral reef.
entries.exAr: يقود *الناشطون البيئيون* حملات منذ سنوات لحماية الشعاب المرجانية.

entries.ex: Burning plastic releases *toxic* fumes that are harmful to breathe.
entries.exAr: يطلق حرق البلاستيك أبخرة *سامة* تضر بمن يستنشقها.

entries.ex: Intensive farming can *degrade* the soil until almost nothing will grow in it.
entries.exAr: قد تؤدي الزراعة المكثفة إلى *تدهور* التربة حتى لا يكاد ينمو فيها شيء.

entries.ex: The government has created national parks to *preserve* rare plants and animals.
entries.exAr: أنشأت الحكومة محميات وطنية *للحفاظ على* النباتات والحيوانات النادرة.

entries.ex: The ban on certain chemicals has allowed the *ozone layer* to begin recovering.
entries.exAr: سمح حظر بعض المواد الكيميائية *لطبقة الأوزون* بأن تبدأ في التعافي.

entries.ex: Overgrazing and drought have accelerated *desertification* in parts of Africa.
entries.exAr: سرّع الرعي الجائر والجفاف وتيرة *التصحر* في أجزاء من أفريقيا.

entries.ex: On some winter days, thick *smog* makes it hard to see the buildings across the river.
entries.exAr: في بعض أيام الشتاء، يجعل *الضباب الدخاني* الكثيف رؤية المباني على الضفة الأخرى من النهر صعبة.

entries.ex: More shoppers are choosing *eco-friendly* products, such as refillable bottles.
entries.exAr: يختار مزيد من المتسوقين منتجات *صديقة للبيئة*، مثل العبوات القابلة لإعادة التعبئة.

entries.ex: Many cafés now offer a discount to customers who avoid *disposable* cups.
entries.exAr: تقدم مقاهٍ كثيرة الآن خصمًا للزبائن الذين يستغنون عن الأكواب *ذات الاستعمال الواحد*.

entries.ex: *Acid rain*, caused by sulphur emissions from power stations, damaged forests across Europe.
entries.exAr: ألحقت *الأمطار الحمضية*، الناجمة عن الكبريت المنبعث من محطات الطاقة، أضرارًا بالغابات في أنحاء أوروبا.

entries.ex: Volunteers collected two tonnes of *litter* from the beach in a single day.
entries.exAr: جمع متطوعون طنين من *القمامة* من الشاطئ في يوم واحد.

entries.ex: Rising *sea levels* threaten low-lying islands in the Pacific.
entries.exAr: يهدد ارتفاع *مستوى سطح البحر* الجزر المنخفضة في المحيط الهادئ.

entries.ex: Planting trees in cities can *mitigate* the effects of extreme heat.
entries.exAr: يمكن لزراعة الأشجار في المدن أن *تخفف* من آثار الحر الشديد.

entries.ex: Earthquakes are among the deadliest *natural disasters* because they strike without warning.
entries.exAr: تُعد الزلازل من أشد *الكوارث الطبيعية* فتكًا لأنها تقع دون سابق إنذار.

gap.s: Around half of the city's rubbish still ends up in ____ rather than being burned for energy.
The new law requires power stations to reduce their ____ of sulphur dioxide.
Farmers lost most of their wheat during the ____, when it did not rain for eight months.
Residents are encouraged to ____ old electronic devices at special collection points.
Lead is a ____ metal that can harm children's brains even in small amounts.
Coastal cities are building sea walls to ____ the risk of flooding.
The charity works to ____ ancient woodlands for future generations.
A ban on ____ plastic cutlery came into force last year.

para.a: The amount of carbon dioxide that each person produces is getting bigger.
para.b: The average person's *carbon footprint* is steadily growing.

para.a: Cutting down forests is making many animals lose their homes.
para.b: *Deforestation* is destroying the habitats of many species.

para.a: The air in big cities is often dirty and full of smoke.
para.b: Many major cities suffer from heavy *smog* and poor air quality.

para.a: We need ways of living that do not harm the planet in the long term.
para.b: We need to adopt more *sustainable* lifestyles to protect the planet.

p1.q: Is there much pollution where you live?
p1.a: Unfortunately, yes. I live in a busy city, and during rush hour the traffic creates quite a lot of *smog*. It's improved slightly since the new metro opened, but air *pollution* is still a real problem.

We try to. We separate paper and plastic bottles, and my mother takes them to the *recycling* bins near the supermarket. We've also stopped buying *disposable* plates, which has cut our rubbish quite noticeably.

p1.q: Do you enjoy spending time in nature?
p1.a: Very much. Whenever I get the chance, I go hiking in the mountains outside my city. Being surrounded by trees and fresh air helps me relax, and it reminds me why we need to *preserve* these places.

p2.cue: Describe something you do to help protect the environment.
points: how easy or difficult it is
and explain why you think it is important
p2.a: Something I've been doing for about two years now is cutting down on single-use plastic. It started after I watched a documentary about plastic in the ocean, which showed sea turtles that had swallowed bags because they looked like jellyfish. I found it so upsetting that I decided to change my habits straight away. In practice, I carry a refillable water bottle and a cloth shopping bag wherever I go, and I refuse *disposable* cups and straws in cafés. I've also started buying *eco-friendly* products with less packaging, such as bars of soap instead of liquid soap in plastic bottles. To be honest, it isn't always easy. Sometimes I forget my bag, and some products are only sold wrapped in plastic. However, it soon becomes a habit. I think it's important because most plastic is never recycled; it either ends up in *landfill* or in the sea, where it can take centuries to *degrade*. If millions of people made small changes like this, the overall impact on the planet would be enormous.

p3.q: Who should be mainly responsible for protecting the environment: governments or individuals?
p3.a: I'd say governments carry the greater responsibility, because they can pass laws that affect millions of people at once, for example by taxing carbon *emissions* or investing in public transport. Individuals matter too, of course, but personal choices are limited if the cleaner options are expensive or unavailable. So the most effective approach is for governments to make the *sustainable* choice the easy and affordable one.

p3.q: How do you think climate change will affect people's lives in the next fifty years?
p3.a: I suspect the impact will be felt most through extreme weather. Many regions will probably face more frequent heatwaves, *droughts* and floods, which could push up food prices and force some communities to move. Coastal cities may need expensive defences against rising *sea levels*. On the positive side, the pressure to adapt could speed up innovation in clean energy and water technology.

writing.q: In many cities, the amount of household waste is increasing rapidly. What are the main causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to solve it? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
essay: In many cities around the world, the volume of rubbish produced by households is rising at an alarming rate. This essay will argue that the problem stems mainly from a culture of convenience and from weak *waste* management systems, and that a combination of government regulation and public education offers the best solution.

The first major cause is the growing reliance on *disposable* products. Busy lifestyles mean that many people buy ready meals, takeaway coffee and online deliveries, all of which come with layers of packaging that are used once and then thrown away. A second cause is the lack of proper infrastructure. In numerous cities, there are no separate bins for paper, glass or plastic, so even residents who want to *recycle* find it difficult, and most rubbish is simply sent to *landfill*, where some items release *toxic* chemicals into the soil.

Several measures could tackle this issue. Governments could charge manufacturers a fee for excessive packaging, which would encourage them to design *eco-friendly* alternatives. Local authorities should also provide convenient recycling collections and food waste bins, as many European cities have done successfully. Finally, public campaigns and school programmes could teach people to reduce, reuse and repair, since small changes in daily habits, such as carrying a refillable bottle, can significantly lower the amount of plastic that ends up in the environment.

In conclusion, the rise in household waste is largely caused by convenience-based consumption and inadequate recycling facilities. By making producers responsible for their packaging and making recycling easy for residents, cities can *mitigate* this problem and move towards a more *sustainable* future.
